Findings:
> The contour of anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments appearing within normal limit
> No definite tear of medial or lateral meniscus in this study
> Normal appearance of medial and lateral collateral ligaments
> No significant bone marrow edema or active cortical destruction in distal femur, proximal tibia and fibula in this study.
> Minimal joint effusion

Impression:

Zentrierte Stellung im Kniegelenk. Patella zentriert. Gering suprapatellarer Erguss. Kein wesentliches Knochenmarksödem. Bis kraniokaudal 2,1 cm messende Läsion in der Tibiametaphyse gelegen mit randständiger Mehrsklerosierung und zentral fettisointensem Signal (5/25), keine kortikale Arrosion oder malignomsuspekte Stigmata. 
Unauffälliger Knorpelbesatz retropatellar und femorotibial. Intakte Darstellung des vorderen und hinteren Kreuzbandes, intakte Kollateralbänder. Geringe Signalanhebung bei mukoider Degeneration des Innenmeniskushinterhorns (6/7). Intakte Darstellung und Konfiguration des Außenmeniskus. Intakte Darstellung von Quadriceps- und Patellarsehne. Keine wesentliche Chondropathie femorotibial. Unauffällige Signalgebung der Muskulatur und subkutanen Weichgewebe.

MRI of right knee with SG PD FatSat, SG T2W FS, SG T1W, CO T2W FS, AX T2W FS

* A space-occupying lobulated cystic lesion in popliteal fossa, extended from the tendons of the medial head of the gastrocnemius, showing hypointense in T1WI and hyperintense in T2WI and internal septums. R/O ganglion cyst. Differential diagnosis of synovial cyst, more than 6 cm in length..
> The contour of ACL & PCL appear to be within normal, no abnormal signal intensity is noted.
> No evidence of tear is noted in either medial or lateral meniscus in this study.
> Both medial & lateral collateral ligaments appear to be within normal.
> No significant bone marrow edema or active cortical destruction noted at distal femur and proximal tibia and fibula in this study.
> Spur formation and tiny subchondral cyst at femoral  trochlea, in favor of mild degneeration.

Impression:
1. Right popliteal cystic lesion, R/O ganglion cyst or bursal cyst along medial head of the gastrocnemius muscle/ tendon.
2. R/O mild degeneration of knee joint.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation.

MRI of left Knee with 
-SG PD FatSat, Locator, SG T2W FS, SG T1W, CO T2W FS, AX T2W FS

* Interstitial intermediate signal in ACL on T2WI, R/O grade 1 injury.
* There are linear signal intensity in posterior horn of medial meniscus, it extends into the surface, in favor of tear.
* The contour of LCL is not in straight and with interstitila signal on T2WI FS, in favor of tear
* Large amount of joint effusion and suprapatellar and infrapatellar bursitis with suprapatellar plicae and irregularity of Hoffa fat pad; hypertrophy of the synovium, indicative of synovitis.
* Wearing of articular cartilage of knee and tiny spur and subchondral cyst, more severe at medial compartment. 
> No significant bone marrow edema or active cortical destruction noted at distal femur and proximal tibia and fibula in this study.
> No significant myositis noted at distal thights to proximal legs.
> The contour of  PCL appear to be within normal, no abnormal signal intensity is noted.
> No evidence of bone contusion is noted.
> Subcutaneous infiltration around knee, more prominent at  infrapatellar region.
Impression:
1. C/W osteoarthritis of left knee, more prominent at medial compartment.
2. Degeneration of medial  meniscus and tear of posterior horn of medial meniscus
3. Synovitis of left knee with suprapatellar bursitis 
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation.

Clinical information: Stiffness in the left knee after tripped on street and banged on cement. Rule out fat pad impingement or meniscal pathology.

Technique: Unenhanced multiplanar multiphase MRI of the left knee performed and 3.0 Tesla MRI scanner.

Findings:
There is a complex degenerative tearing of the posterior horn of the medial meniscus extending into the tibial meniscal surface. There is slight meniscal extrusion. The lateral meniscus is intact.

The cruciate and collateral ligaments are intact. Extensor mechanism of the knee is unremarkable.

There are no deep cartilage defects in the medial and lateral femorotibial joint compartment. There are no deep cartilage defects in the patellofemoral joint compartment. There is patchy bone marrow edema involving the midportion and inferior patellar pole without focal fracture line.

The infrapatellar fat pad is unremarkable. There is mild joint effusion. There are no intra-articular bodies. There is a low volume Baker's cyst.

The visualized muscle bulk is unremarkable.

Conclusion:
1. Patchy bone marrow edema at the inferior patellar pole without focal fracture line, most probably representing bone contusion after a previous trauma.
2. Degenerative tearing of the medial meniscus as described in detail above.
3. No deep cartilage defects.

-3-Plane Loc, Sag PD FS, Sag T2 FS, Sag T1, Cor T2 FS, Ax T2 FS

* Focal mildly increased signal intensity in posterior horn of lateral meniscus on F/S PD sequence  (srs: 4, Img:13), but not visible on F/S T2WI, , maybe due to mortion artifact
* Equal-sized medial and lateral facets of the patella, reflecting Wiberg type I patella.
   Mild wearing of articular cartilage of patella and femoral trochlea, R/O grade 2 chondromalacia. No signficant subchondral bone marrow edema or cysts.
* Subcutaneous infiltration over infrapatellar region.
> No significant bone marrow edema or active cortical destruction noted at distal femur and proximal tibia and fibula in this study.
> The contour of ACL & PCL appear to be within normal, no abnormal signal intensity is noted.
> No significant myositis noted at distal thights to proximal legs.
> No evidence of tear is noted in medial meniscus in this study.
> Lateral collateral ligaments appear to be within normal.
> No evidence of bone contusion is noted.
> Interstitial increased signal intensity of quadriceps tendon without thickening, maybe due to normal striated appearance of the distal quadriceps tendon on F/S T2WI; differential diagnosis of  tendinosis.
> Mild subchondral hypointensity area in lateral femoral condyle on T1WI, in favor of mild subchondral sclerosis.
> No significant increased joint effusion of left knee joint.

Impression:
1. R/O grade 2 chondromalacia of left patellofemoral joint.
2. Mild subcutaneous edema over infrapatellar region.

Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE RIGHT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: Anterior knee pain for 10 months
Comparison: No relevant prior studies available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the right knee was performed on a 1.5 Tesla system with a dedicated knee coil in three planes (axial, sagittal, and coronal), using a standard non-contrast protocol.

FINDINGS:

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
There is a mild patella alto configuration at the right knee.
No fracture. No evidence for a recent pivot shift mechanism.
There is ill-defined bone marrow edema in the lateral body of the patella compatible with osseous stress response across the extensor mechanism.
Bone marrow signal is otherwise normal.

JOINT SPACE:
Small right knee effusion.
Minimal Baker's cyst.
No intra-articular bodies.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Medial compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: Normal in morphology and signal.
Lateral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
Patellofemoral compartment cartilage: No focal cartilage defects.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): Normal.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: Normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Normal.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Patella tendon: No tendinosis or tear.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: Edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad, with mild reactive patellar marrow edema laterally. No lateral patellar tilt or translation. Mild patella alta. Normal patellar and trochlear morphology. Normal tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance measuring 10 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
No acute muscle strain or muscle atrophy. Visualized tendons not previously discussed are intact without tendinosis or tear.

SOFT TISSUES:
No soft tissue mass. Normal popliteal neurovascular bundle.

IMPRESSION:
Findings of active lateral patella maltracking, with edema in superolateral Hoffa's fat pad, and osseous stress response in the lateral body of the patella.
